record.original_question: Can one develop an algorithmic procedure that converts generalized Kirby diagrams representing non-orientable 1-handles into gems of the corresponding 4-manifolds? In addition, do the resulting gems admit gem-induced trisections in enough generality that gem methods would then provide an estimation of trisection genus for all closed 4-manifolds, including the non-orientable setting?

evidence.quote: As regards Section 3.1, an interesting development would be to obtain an algorithmic procedure to pass from Kirby diagrams to gems in the generalized case of diagrams representing also non-orientable 1-handles (according to [19]).

If the resulting gems admitted gem-induced trisections (as happens in the orientable setting: see Theorem 17), in virtue of the non-orientable version of Laudenbach-Poenaru's result due to [32], an estimation of the trisection genus for all closed 4-manifolds would be obtained, via gems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions:

(a) A gem (graph-encoded manifold) of dimension 4 is a 5-edge-colored multigraph (Γ, γ) with γ: E(Γ) → {0,1,2,3,4} such that edges incident to any vertex receive five distinct colors, and Γ encodes a closed PL 4-manifold M(Γ) via the standard construction that associates an n-simplex to each vertex and glues simplices along facets according to the coloring.

(b) A generalized Kirby diagram for a closed PL 4-manifold is the standard Kirby calculus description extended to allow non-orientable 1-handles (i.e., 1-handles attached so that the resulting 2-handlebody may be non-orientable), with framings on 2-handles given in this generalized setting.

(c) A trisection of a closed PL 4-manifold M is a decomposition M = X₁ ∪ X₂ ∪ X₃ where each Xᵢ is a 4-dimensional 1-handlebody, pairwise intersections are 3-dimensional handlebodies, and the triple intersection is a closed surface Σ; the trisection genus g(M) is the minimum genus of Σ over all trisections of M. This notion extends to the non-orientable setting using the non-orientable analogue of the Laudenbach–Poénaru theorem.

(d) A gem (Γ, γ) is said to admit a gem-induced trisection of M(Γ) if a canonical trisection of M(Γ) can be read directly from the combinatorics of (Γ, γ).

Problem:

(1) Construct an explicit algorithm that, given a generalized Kirby diagram K (allowing non-orientable 1-handles) representing a closed PL 4-manifold M, produces a 5-colored gem (Γ_K, γ_K) such that M(Γ_K) is PL-homeomorphic to M.

(2) Prove or disprove: for every closed PL 4-manifold M (orientable or non-orientable), the gem (Γ_K, γ_K) produced by such an algorithm admits a gem-induced trisection, so that minimizing the genus of gem-induced trisections over gems associated to generalized Kirby diagrams of M yields a finite upper bound for the trisection genus g(M).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open development in a 2025 review on Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds. While related results exist—algorithms taking Kirby diagrams to trisection diagrams in the orientable case, an extension of Bell–Hass–Rubinstein–Tillmann's triangulation-based trisection algorithm to non-orientable 4-manifolds, and an extension of gem-induced trisections to non-orientable compact 4-manifolds via colored triangulations—no source found gives a direct algorithm from generalized Kirby diagrams (with non-orientable 1-handles) to gems together with gem-induced trisections yielding trisection genus estimates for all closed 4-manifolds. The specific combined problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds: relationships, results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Gem theory has interesting interactions with classical Kirby diagrams and trisections; algorithmic procedures and open problems are discussed.
status_evidence.claim: The combined algorithmic problem is listed among open developments.

status_evidence.title: Trisections of PL 4-manifolds arising from colored triangulations
status_evidence.snippet: Notion of gem-induced trisection extended to non-orientable compact 4-manifolds from colored triangulations.
status_evidence.claim: Gem-induced trisections have been extended to the non-orientable setting, providing partial progress.

status_evidence.title: An Algorithm taking Kirby diagrams to Trisection diagrams
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm from Kirby diagrams to trisection diagrams in the orientable case.
status_evidence.claim: An orientable-case algorithm exists, but the non-orientable Kirby-to-gem version is not established.

status_evidence.title: Determining the Trisection Genus of Orientable and Non-Orientable PL 4-Manifolds through Triangulations
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm to compute trisections from triangulations extended to non-orientable 4-manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Triangulation-based methods exist for non-orientable 4-manifolds, but not via generalized Kirby-diagram-to-gem conversion.
